doc.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: Recordings: That Old Gang of Mine and Melancholy Baby
summary: Rowe plays a track with Dan Barrett; Masso describes his Arbors album and the bossa nova Melancholy Baby.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah. I was going to play a little something for you, and get your comment on this.
[audio interlude]
I assume you recognize that.
I sure do.
Your latest? Is this your latest recording?
No, it’s not. No. This is the one with Dan Barrett?
Dan Barrett, yeah.
Yeah. “Let’s Be Buddies.”
Yeah.

I have one that was just released, and I call it “That Old Gang of Mine.” It’s on Arbors. And it’s all players from the southern New England area that I grew up with, with the exception of Marshall Wood, the bassist, but he’s such a good player, he had to be on it. I’ve known Marshall at least ten years. But the other guys I’ve known for about 40 years and I’ve been wanting to do this. It’s Dick Johnson, Lou Columbo — are you familiar with that name? Dave McKenna, Marshall Wood, Artie Cabral, a drummer from Providence, and myself. It’s a sextet. And it really is, it’s that old gang of mine, and I was just so happy that Arbors let me do it, and in fact they got behind me a hundred percent and just gave me carte blanche.
Wow. That’s a good label. I mean they really are supporting this kind of music, whatever it is.
Who knows? Why do we have to name it?
I know. Isn’t that something? But this particular tune, “Melancholy Baby,” what made you think of doing it, as a sort of samba?

It’s a beautiful tune. And I just, I do love to do things as a bossa nova, and I’m constantly thinking of what tune might be good in that context. And “Melancholy Baby,” I thought I would give it a try. I play the verse on that too, which is really beautiful.
Yeah. When it first started out I’m going, this isn’t the “Melancholy Baby” I know. I don’t think I ever heard the verse before.
A lot of people haven’t.
Of course we always associate that tune with the drunken request I think.
I know.
But actually no one ever asked me for that.
I haven’t had that experience either, but the joke is as old as the hills.
